correctness.rationale: For fixed x>0 and even N, the Macdonald integral equals a strictly log-concave positive moment with one saddle. Saddle equation, curvature and third/fourth derivatives are exact. On the centered Gaussian scale, cubic terms have order sqrt(t/N), quartic terms order t/N; all odd Gaussian contributions cancel, and the remainder is O((t/N)^2) after explicit finite moments. Tails are exponentially negligible by local uniform concavity and one-sided monotonicity. The limit of N Q_N/t_N is -1/8+5/24=1/12. Finite SciPy checker replays centered moment quadrature at twelve parameter-index pairs and is diagnostic, not an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The motivating 2026 numerical paper explicitly tackles very high order derivatives of Macdonald K. This theorem supplies a controlled two-term large-index expansion, resolves the leading nonzero relative correction exactly (1/12), and explains both scaling via Lambert W and how Gaussian-only approximations err by order log N/N. It is a natural invariant of the canonical ν=0 even-derivative moments rather than a selected ad hoc finite sample. This goes beyond reproducing an integral or routine finite low-order derivative.
